summary: The Megillah may be read standing or sitting, by one or two people. On Monday, Thursday and Shabbos Minchah, three people are called up to the Torah.

chunks.en: One who reads the Megillah may stand or sit.
chunks.st: One who reads the Megilla may position himself as he wishes, either standing or sitting.

chunks.en: If one person read it,
chunks.st: Whether one person reads the Megilla

chunks.en: or two read it together,
chunks.st: or two people read it together,

chunks.en: they have done the mitzvah. In a place where people usually make a bracha,
chunks.st: they have fulfilled their obligation. In a place where the people are accustomed to recite a blessing over the reading,

chunks.en: he makes a bracha. And where they don't,
chunks.st: one should recite a blessing. And in a place where it is customary not to recite a blessing,

chunks.en: he does not make a bracha.
chunks.st: one should not recite a blessing.
chunks.stMore: The mishna records several laws governing public Torah readings.

chunks.en: On Monday, Thursday, and Shabbos at Minchah,
chunks.st: On Mondays and Thursdays during the morning service and on Shabbat during the afternoon service,

chunks.en: three people read from the Torah,
chunks.st: three people read from the Torah;

chunks.en: no fewer and no more,
chunks.st: one may neither decrease the number of readers nor add to them.

chunks.en: and there is no haftarah from the Nevi'im.
chunks.explain: The haftarah is a reading from the Nevi'im after the Torah reading.
chunks.st: And one does not conclude with a reading from the Prophets [haftara] on these occasions.

chunks.en: The one who starts and the one who ends the Torah reading
chunks.st: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah

chunks.en: make a bracha before it and after it.
chunks.explain: The first one says the bracha before, and the last one says the bracha after.
chunks.st: recite a blessing; one recites before the beginning of the reading and one recites after its conclusion, but the middle reader does not recite a blessing.

summary: This mishnah teaches how many people are called up to the Torah: four on Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed, five on Yom Tov, six on Yom Kippur, and seven on Shabbos.

chunks.en: On Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed,
chunks.st: On the days of the New Moon and on the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: four people read,
chunks.st: four people read from the Torah;

chunks.he: אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן,
chunks.en: no fewer and no more,
chunks.st: one may neither decrease the number of readers nor add to them.

chunks.en: and there is no haftarah from the Nevi'im.
chunks.st: And one does not conclude with a reading from the Prophets.

chunks.en: The one who starts and the one who ends the Torah reading
chunks.st: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah

chunks.en: make a bracha before it and after it.
chunks.st: recite a blessing. The first reader recites a blessing before the beginning of the reading, and the last reader recites a blessing after its conclusion, but the middle readers do not recite a blessing.
chunks.stMore: The mishna formulates a general principle with regard to the number of people who read from the Torah on different occasions.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: Any day that has Mussaf
chunks.st: Any day on which there is an additional offering sacrificed in the Temple

chunks.en: and is not Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and that is not a Festival,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the New Moon and the intermediate days of a Festival,

chunks.en: four people read.
chunks.st: four people read from the Torah;

chunks.en: On Yom Tov,
chunks.st: on a Festival,

chunks.en: five. On Yom Kippur,
chunks.st: five people read; on Yom Kippur,

chunks.en: six. On Shabbos,
chunks.st: six people read; and on Shabbat,

chunks.en: seven. We may not have fewer than them,
chunks.st: seven people read. One may not decrease the number of readers,

chunks.en: but we may add to them,
chunks.st: but one may add to them.

chunks.en: and there is a haftarah from the Nevi'im.
chunks.st: And on these days one concludes with a reading from the Prophets.

chunks.en: The one who starts and the one who ends the Torah reading
chunks.st: Both the one who begins the reading and the one who concludes the reading from the Torah

chunks.en: make a bracha before it and after it.
chunks.st: recite a blessing; one recites before the beginning of the reading and one recites after its conclusion, but the middle readers do not recite a blessing.

summary: Some parts of davening and other things need a minyan of ten men. Also, holy land is valued by ten people, nine and a Kohen.

chunks.en: We do not start the Shema brachos for others,
chunks.explain: One says Barchu and the first bracha before Shema for the people.
chunks.st: One does not recite the introductory prayers and blessing [poresin] before Shema;

chunks.en: and nobody goes before the aron to lead davening,
chunks.st: nor does one pass before the ark to repeat the Amida prayer;

chunks.en: and the Kohanim do not lift their hands,
chunks.explain: To say Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: nor do the priests lift their hands to recite the Priestly Benediction;

chunks.en: and we do not read from the Torah,
chunks.st: nor is the Torah read in public;

chunks.en: and there is no haftarah from the Nevi'im,
chunks.st: nor does one conclude with a reading from the Prophets [haftara] in the presence of fewer than ten men.

chunks.en: and we do not do the standing and sitting at a funeral,
chunks.st: And one does not observe the practice of standing up and sitting down for the delivery of eulogies at a funeral service;

chunks.en: and we do not say the mourners' bracha,
chunks.st: nor does one recite the mourners’ blessing or

chunks.en: or comfort the mourners, or say the chassan's brachos,
chunks.explain: The chassan's brachos are the Sheva Brachos at a wedding.
chunks.st: comfort mourners in two lines after the funeral; or recite the bridegrooms’ blessing;

chunks.en: and we do not say "Let us bless our G-d" in bentching
chunks.st: and one does not invite others to recite Grace after Meals, i.e., conduct a zimmun, with the name of God,

chunks.en: with fewer than ten.
chunks.st: with fewer than ten men present.

chunks.en: And for land, nine and a Kohen.
chunks.explain: Ten people, one a Kohen, decide how much holy land is worth.
chunks.st: If one consecrated land and now wishes to redeem it, the land must be assessed by nine men and one priest, for a total of ten.

chunks.en: And the same for a person.
chunks.explain: When someone promised his own value to the Beis HaMikdash.
chunks.st: And similarly, assessing the value of a person who has pledged his own value to the Temple must be undertaken by ten people, one of whom must be a priest.

summary: The Torah reader must read at least three pesukim, and gives the translator only one pasuk at a time. In the Navi we may skip around a little, but not in the Torah.

chunks.he: הַקּוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה לֹא יִפְחֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְסוּקִים.
chunks.en: One who reads in the Torah may not read fewer than three pesukim.
chunks.st: One who reads from the Torah in the synagogue should not read fewer than three verses.

chunks.he: לֹא יִקְרָא לַמְּתֻרְגְּמָן יוֹתֵר מִפָּסוּק אֶחָד,
chunks.en: He may not read more than one pasuk at a time to the translator,
chunks.explain: The translator said each pasuk in Aramaic for everyone.
chunks.st: And when it is being translated, he should not read to the translator more than one verse at a time,
chunks.stMore: so that the translator will not become confused.

chunks.en: and in the Navi, three.
chunks.st: And with regard to the Prophets, one may read to the translator three verses at a time.
chunks.stMore: With respect to the Torah, an incorrect translation might lead to an error in practice, but this concern does not apply to the Prophets.

chunks.en: If the three were three separate parshiyos,
chunks.st: If the three verses constitute three separate paragraphs,
chunks.stMore: that is to say, if each verse is a paragraph in itself,

chunks.en: he reads them one by one.
chunks.st: one must read them to the translator one by one.

chunks.en: We may skip around in the Navi, but we may not skip in the Torah.
chunks.st: One may skip from one place to another while reading the Prophets, but one may not skip from one place to another while reading the Torah.

chunks.en: And how far may he skip?
chunks.st: How far may he skip?

chunks.en: As far as he can before the translator finishes.
chunks.explain: The people should not have to wait for him.
chunks.st: As far as he can, provided that the translator will not conclude his translation while the reader is still rolling the scroll to the new location. The reader may not cause the congregation to wait for him after the translator has finished, as that would be disrespectful to the congregation.

summary: The one who reads the haftarah gets the honor of saying the Shema brachos, leading davening and duchening if he is a Kohen. If he is a child, his father or rebbi leads instead.

chunks.en: The one who reads the haftarah from the Navi,
chunks.st: The one who concludes with a reading from the Prophets [haftara]

words.en: the one who reads the haftarah

chunks.en: he starts the Shema brachos,
chunks.st: is also the one who is honored to recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

chunks.en: and he leads the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: and he passes before the ark to repeat the Amida prayer,

chunks.en: and he lifts his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and if he is a priest he lifts his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: And if he was a child,
chunks.st: And if the one who reads the haftara is a minor,
chunks.stMore: who may read the haftara but is not qualified to lead the congregation in prayer,

chunks.he: אָבִיו אוֹ רַבּוֹ עוֹבְרִין עַל יָדוֹ:
chunks.en: his father or his rebbi leads the davening in his place.
chunks.st: his father or teacher is honored to pass before the ark in his place.

summary: A child may read the Torah but may not lead the davening. A person in torn clothes may not read the Torah or lead. A blind person may still say the brachos of Shema, but Rabbi Yehudah disagrees about someone blind from birth.

chunks.en: A child may read from the Torah and translate it,
chunks.st: A minor may read the Torah in public and also translate the text for the congregation into Aramaic,

chunks.en: but he may not start the Shema brachos,
chunks.st: but he may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema,

chunks.en: and he may not lead the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: and he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer,

chunks.en: and he may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.st: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: A person in torn clothes may start the Shema brachos and translate,
chunks.explain: His clothes are torn so his arms show.
chunks.st: One whose limbs are exposed [poḥe’aḥ] may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema and translate the Torah reading into Aramaic,

words.note: A person whose clothes are torn.

chunks.en: but he may not read from the Torah,
chunks.explain: Out of respect for the Torah.
chunks.st: but he may not read from the Torah out of respect for the Torah;

chunks.en: and he may not lead the davening before the aron,
chunks.st: he may not pass before the ark to lead the congregation in prayer;

chunks.en: and he may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.explain: Out of respect for the people.
chunks.st: and he may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction out of respect for the congregation.

chunks.en: A blind person may start the Shema brachos and translate.
chunks.st: One who is blind may recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema, and he may also translate the Torah reading into Aramaic.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: anyone who never saw the lights in his life,
chunks.explain: The sun, moon and stars. He was blind from birth.
chunks.st: Anyone who has not seen the luminaries, the sun, moon, and stars, in his life, i.e., he was blind from birth,

chunks.en: may not start the Shema brachos.
chunks.explain: The first bracha before Shema is about the lights.
chunks.st: may not recite the introductory prayers and blessing before Shema. The first of the blessings before Shema is the blessing over the luminaries, and one who has never seen them cannot recite the blessing at all.

summary: A Kohen with marks on his hands may not duchen, because people will look at his hands. Rabbi Yehudah says the same about a Kohen whose hands are dyed blue or red.

chunks.en: A Kohen who has blemishes on his hands
chunks.st: A priest who has blemishes on his hands

words.note: Marks or problems on the body.

chunks.en: may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim.
chunks.explain: People would look at his hands, and we may not look then.
chunks.st: may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction.
chunks.stMore: Because of his blemish, people will look at his hands, and it is prohibited to look at the hands of the priests during the Priestly Benediction.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even one whose hands were
chunks.st: Even one whose hands were

chunks.en: colored with blue or red dye,
chunks.st: colored with satis, a blue dye,

chunks.en: may not lift his hands for Birkas Kohanim,
chunks.st: may not lift his hands to recite the Priestly Benediction

chunks.en: because the people will look at him.
chunks.st: because the congregation will look at him.

summary: Someone who insists on wearing special clothes or shoes to lead davening may not lead at all. Tefillin must be square and worn in the right place, the way the Sages taught.

chunks.he: הָאוֹמֵר אֵינִי עוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּבָה בִצְבוּעִין,
chunks.en: One who says, I won't lead davening in colored clothes,
chunks.st: One who says: I will not pass before the ark to lead the prayer service in colored garments,

chunks.en: may not lead even in white clothes.
chunks.explain: We worry he does not follow the ways of the Sages.
chunks.st: may not pass before the ark to lead the prayer service even in white garments.
chunks.stMore: There is concern that one who insists on wearing clothing of a specific color during his prayers is a heretic and therefore unfit to lead the service.

chunks.en: If he says, I won't lead in sandals,
chunks.st: Similarly, if one says: I will not pass before the ark wearing sandals,

chunks.en: he may not lead even barefoot.
chunks.st: he may not pass before it even barefoot,
chunks.stMore: as he is not acting in accordance with the teachings of the Sages.

chunks.en: One who makes his tefillin round,
chunks.st: One who constructs his phylacteries in a round shape

chunks.en: it is dangerous and it is not a mitzvah.
chunks.explain: Tefillin must be square.
chunks.st: exposes himself to danger during times of persecution, when foreign governments impose a ban on the mitzva of phylacteries, and yet he does not fulfill the mitzva to don phylacteries,

chunks.en: If he put them on his forehead
chunks.explain: The head tefillin go above where the hair starts.
chunks.st: If one placed the phylacteries worn on the head on his forehead, and not in its proper place above his hairline,

chunks.en: or on his palm,
chunks.explain: The hand tefillin go on the upper arm.
chunks.st: or if he placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on his palm, and not on his bicep,

chunks.en: this is the way of the minim.
chunks.explain: Minim are people who don't believe in the teachings of the Sages.
chunks.st: this is the way of the heretics,
chunks.stMore: i.e., those who reject the tradition of the Sages with regard to the proper placement of the phylacteries.

words.note: People who don't believe in the Sages' teachings.

chunks.en: If he covered them with gold,
chunks.st: If one plated his phylacteries with gold

chunks.en: or put the hand tefillin on his sleeve,
chunks.st: or placed the phylacteries worn on the arm on the outside of his sleeve [unkeli],

chunks.en: this is the way of the outsiders.
chunks.explain: People who don't follow the ways of the Jewish people.
chunks.st: this is the way of the outsiders, i.e., those who do not take part in the traditions of the Jewish people.

summary: Some words in davening sound like wrong beliefs, so we stop the person who says them. We also stop a person who changes the meaning of the Torah when reading or translating it.

chunks.en: One who says, "The good people will bless You,"
chunks.explain: We daven together with everyone, not only the good people.
chunks.st: If one says in his prayers: May the good bless You,

chunks.en: this is the way of the minim.
chunks.st: this is a path of heresy,
chunks.stMore: as heretics divide the world into two domains, good and evil.

chunks.en: Or says, "Your mercy reaches the bird's nest,"
chunks.explain: The mitzvah of sending away the mother bird before taking the eggs.
chunks.st: If one says the following in his prayers: Just as Your mercy is extended to a bird’s nest,
chunks.stMore: as You have commanded us to send away the mother before taking her chicks or eggs (see Deuteronomy 22:6–7), so too extend Your mercy to us;

chunks.en: or "For the good may Your name be mentioned,"
chunks.st: or: May Your name be mentioned with the good;

chunks.en: or "We thank, we thank,"
chunks.explain: Saying it twice.
chunks.st: or: We give thanks, we give thanks, twice,

chunks.en: we make him be quiet.
chunks.st: he is suspected of heretical beliefs and they silence him.

chunks.en: One who changes the words of the parshah of forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: If one modifies the text while reading the laws of forbidden sexual relations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he introduces euphemisms out of a sense of propriety,

chunks.en: we make him be quiet.
chunks.st: they silence him.

chunks.en: One who says, "And from your children do not give to pass
chunks.st: Similarly, if one says while translating the verse: “And you shall not give any of your seed to set them apart

chunks.en: to Molech,"
chunks.explain: Molech was an avodah zarah.
chunks.st: to Molekh” (Leviticus 18:21):

chunks.en: and translates it in a different, wrong way,
chunks.st: And you shall not give any of your seed to impregnate an Aramean woman,

words.note: He changed the meaning of the pasuk.

chunks.en: we make him be quiet with a scolding.
chunks.st: he is silenced with rebuke.

summary: Some stories in Tanach are read in shul but not translated, and some are not read at all. Some parts of the Navi are not used for the haftarah.

chunks.en: The story of Reuven
chunks.st: The incident of Reuben, about which it says: “And Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine” (Genesis 35:22),

chunks.en: is read but not translated.
chunks.explain: So people won't think badly of Reuven.
chunks.st: is read from the Torah in public but not translated, so that the uneducated not come to denigrate Reuben.

chunks.en: The story of Tamar
chunks.st: The incident of Tamar (Genesis, chapter 38)

chunks.en: is read and translated.
chunks.st: is read in public and also translated.

chunks.en: The first part of the story of the Golden Calf
chunks.st: The first report of the incident of the Golden Calf, i.e., the Torah’s account of the incident itself (Exodus 32:1–20),

chunks.en: is read and translated.
chunks.st: is read and translated,

chunks.en: And the second part,
chunks.explain: When Aharon tells Moshe what happened.
chunks.st: but the second narrative, i.e., Aaron’s report to Moses of what had taken place (Exodus 32:21–24)

chunks.en: is read but not translated.
chunks.st: is read but not translated.

chunks.en: Birkas Kohanim,
chunks.st: The verses constituting the Priestly Benediction (Numbers 6:24–26)
chunks.basisNote: Bartenura says Birkas Kohanim is read but not translated.

chunks.en: the story of David
chunks.st: and the incident of David

chunks.en: and Amnon,
chunks.st: and Amnon (II Samuel, chapter 13)

chunks.en: are not read and not translated.
chunks.st: are neither read nor translated.

chunks.en: We do not read the Merkavah for a haftarah,
chunks.explain: The Merkavah is Yechezkel's vision of Hashem's chariot.
chunks.st: One may not conclude the Torah reading with by reading from the Prophets the account of the Divine Chariot (Ezekiel, chapter 1),
chunks.stMore: so as not to publicize that which was meant to remain hidden.

chunks.en: but Rabbi Yehudah allows it.
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yehuda permits it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: We do not read for the haftarah
chunks.st: One may not conclude with section from the Prophets beginning with:

chunks.en: "Make known to Yerushalayim."
chunks.explain: It speaks badly about the Jewish people.
chunks.st: “Make known to Jerusalem her abominations” (Ezekiel 16:2), because it speaks derogatively of the Jewish people.
